summary: Join our expert-led training course on flood and drought risk management. Equip yourself with essential strategies to tackle climate challenges effectively.
lede: Flood and drought risk management helps resilience, emergency-response, infrastructure and operations professionals turn climate hazards into practical plans. Participants learn to map exposure and vulnerability, assess flood and drought hotspots, and use climate forecasts and trigger thresholds to guide early action. They also develop contingency procedures and costed risk-reduction plans using tools such as risk registers, standard operating procedures and monitoring indicators.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals who manage climate-related risks and must plan, fund, implement, or evaluate resilience measures.
audience: Disaster risk management and emergency response officers
Climate change adaptation and resilience planners
County/municipal public works, roads, and drainage teams
Water resources, irrigation, and watershed professionals
Agriculture, food security, and livelihoods program staff
Infrastructure and project managers in flood-prone
Supply chain, logistics, and operations managers
modules: Foundations of Flood and Drought Risk in a Changing Climate
Risk Identification and Data for Decision-Making
Flood Risk Assessment and Hotspot Mapping
Drought Risk Assessment and Water Stress Planning
Climate Information and Forecast Use for Practical Planning
Early Warning Systems and Trigger-Based Early Action
Preparedness Planning, Contingency Plans, and Business Continuity
Risk Reduction Measures and Resilient Infrastructure Options
Financing Resilience and Budget Justification for Risk Reduction
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning for Risk Reduction
Capstone: Your Climate Risk Management Toolkit and Action Plan
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of climate-related risks and experience in planning or management roles. Familiarity with disaster risk management concepts is recommended.
